The 1987 Montreal Protocol on Substances that Deplete the Ozone Layer is a global agreement that phases out ozone-depleting substances. The most recent amendment to the Montreal Protocol, the Kigali Amendment, calls for the phasedown of HFCs by 2047. The American Innovation and Manufacturing (AIM) Act 2020 HFC Phasedown5 outlines the phasedown of widely used HFCs over a 15-year schedule. The Act introduces technology-specific restrictions for the transition. It does not require discontinuing systems currently in use, but it does raise awareness about the potentially higher cost of legacy refrigerants. Decisions about equipment design and form factors (the physical design and layout of the equipment6) can reduce refrigerant charge without impacting performance, reduce leakage, and minimize human exposure to dangerous chemicals.7 For example, a monoblock system (e.g., self-contained refrigeration systems that integrate both the condensing and evaporating units within a single piece of equipment) will have less refrigerant charge, and refrigerant is installed by the manufacturer at the factory. Conversely, VRF systems will have more refrigerant charge and will have field-installed equipment that has more opportunity to leak. How To Use This Guide This document can help support a portfolio-wide refrigerant action plan. Through a series of steps, it outlines the information needed to establish a refrigerant inventory, develops refrigerant management goals, and prioritizes actions to achieve those goals. An effective plan measures the current state of refrigerants in a building and provides next steps. These next steps move the organization towards energy goals while strengthening the organization’s business case. The accompanying document [https://www.nlr.gov/docs/fy26osti/95392ActionPlanWorksheet.docx] provides a blank worksheet to help stakeholders document the inventory, goals, and suggested actions in the following five steps: 1. Provide an organizational profile 2. Establish refrigerant management goals 3. Complete a refrigeration equipment inventory 4. Develop a refrigerant charge maintenance inventory 5. Take action.
